hero.title: Discover Palestine through its places and stories.
hero.sub: Explore a growing bilingual guide to Palestinian cities, heritage sites, architecture, and living traditions.

cities.title: Explore the cities
cities.sub: Start with three cities and discover the heritage places held within each one.

hebron.name: Hebron
hebron.summary: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, known for its historic old city, markets, and stone architecture.

bethlehem.name: Bethlehem
bethlehem.summary: A city of pilgrimage, craft, and community, shaped by ancient sacred sites and vibrant neighborhood life.

jerusalem.name: Jerusalem
jerusalem.summary: A layered city of faith, architecture, markets, and communities, with a history visible in every quarter.

citiesPage.title: Explore Palestinian cities
citiesPage.subtitle: Every city holds distinct architecture, traditions, memories, and living cultural practices.

notFound.title: City not found
notFound.hint: The city in this address is not available yet.

ibrahimi-mosque.name: Ibrahimi Mosque
ibrahimi-mosque.description: A major sacred and historic landmark in Hebron's old city.
ibrahimi-mosque.longDescription: The Ibrahimi Mosque stands at the heart of Hebron's historic urban fabric. Its layered architecture reflects centuries of religious, civic, and architectural history.

old-city-market.name: Old City Market
old-city-market.description: Stone alleys, workshops, and shops carrying long-standing local crafts.
old-city-market.longDescription: Hebron's old city market connects homes, workshops, religious sites, and public spaces through a dense network of stone streets and covered passages.

hebron-museum.name: Hebron Museum
hebron-museum.description: A local collection presenting aspects of the city's material heritage.
hebron-museum.longDescription: The museum introduces visitors to objects, photographs, and narratives connected to Hebron's social, architectural, and craft traditions.

church-of-the-nativity.name: Church of the Nativity
church-of-the-nativity.description: A historic Christian pilgrimage site at the center of Bethlehem.
church-of-the-nativity.longDescription: The Church of the Nativity is one of Bethlehem's defining landmarks and forms part of a wider historic landscape of churches, streets, and community institutions.

manger-square.name: Manger Square
manger-square.description: Bethlehem's central civic space, surrounded by religious and cultural landmarks.
manger-square.longDescription: Manger Square functions as a meeting point for residents and visitors, connecting the old city, markets, churches, and public celebrations.

milk-grotto.name: Milk Grotto
milk-grotto.description: A quiet chapel and pilgrimage destination near Bethlehem's old city.
milk-grotto.longDescription: The Milk Grotto is associated with long-standing local and pilgrimage traditions and is known for its pale stone interior and contemplative atmosphere.

al-aqsa-compound.name: Al-Aqsa Compound
al-aqsa-compound.description: A sacred architectural landscape of courtyards, prayer spaces, and historic structures.
al-aqsa-compound.longDescription: The Al-Aqsa compound is a central part of Jerusalem's religious and architectural heritage, bringing together buildings and open spaces from many historical periods.

old-city-alleys.name: Old City Alleys
old-city-alleys.description: A network of historic streets linking neighborhoods, markets, and sacred places.
old-city-alleys.longDescription: Jerusalem's old city alleys reveal the close relationship between domestic life, trade, worship, and architecture within the walled city.

old-city-walls.name: Old City Walls and Gates
old-city-walls.description: Fortifications and gateways that shape the historic city's identity.
old-city-walls.longDescription: The walls and gates define the old city's physical form and remain important points of movement, memory, and orientation.

heritage.title: Heritage places
heritage.sub: Look beyond landmarks to the architecture, craft, memory, and everyday life that give each place meaning.

hero.title: Culture becomes clearer when we look closely.
hero.sub: Culture Lens is a bilingual digital guide designed to organize and share Palestinian cultural heritage through places, images, and accessible stories.

mission.title: Make heritage easier to discover and understand
mission.lead: The project brings city guides, heritage places, and visual material into one clear experience. Its next stage is to grow through careful research, local collaboration, and transparent sourcing.

items.title: Respect
items.description: Present communities, sacred places, and living traditions with care.

items.title: Clarity
items.description: Make cultural information approachable in Arabic and English.

items.title: Context
items.description: Connect buildings and landmarks to the people and histories around them.

items.title: Participation
items.description: Create room for future collaboration with residents, researchers, and cultural institutions.

items.title: Build the foundation
items.description: Create a reliable bilingual city and place structure.

items.title: Verify and source
items.description: Review cultural copy with credible references and local expertise.

items.title: Expand the map
items.description: Add more cities, places, photographs, and thematic journeys.

items.title: Invite contribution
items.description: Develop a reviewed workflow for community stories and images.

end.title: Help shape the next chapter
end.sub: Have a research lead, partnership idea, or cultural contribution?

hero.sub: Questions, research leads, cultural contributions, and partnership ideas are welcome.
